title: Organ Systems Working Together
competency: Trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work; explain how body systems work together such as digestion and excretion; and describe how plant organs work together as a transport system.
objectives: Trace the path of food through the digestive tract.
Explain the processes of mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination.
Describe how the digestive and excretory systems work together for organism survival.
Explain the transport system in plants involving leaves, stems, and roots.
introduction: Living organisms are complex systems where different parts work together to ensure growth and survival. In humans, we process nutrients and eliminate waste through coordinated organ systems. Similarly, plants have specialized organs that function as a transport system to move water and nutrients.
content:
1. The Human Digestive System

Food undergoes a journey through the digestive tract, involving several key processes:

  • Mechanical Processing: Physical breakdown of food (e.g., chewing in the mouth).
  • Secretion: Release of enzymes and fluids to aid digestion.
  • Digestion: Chemical breakdown of food into smaller molecules.
  • Absorption: Nutrients moving from the digestive tract into the bloodstream.
  • Elimination: Removal of undigested food as waste.

2. Coordinating Digestion and Excretion

Body systems do not work in isolation. While the Digestive System breaks down food and absorbs nutrients, the Excretory System (including the kidneys and skin) works to remove metabolic wastes and excess water produced by cells after they use those nutrients. Together, they maintain homeostasis (internal balance).

3. Plant Transport System

Plants lack a heart or blood, but they have organs that work together to move materials:

  • Roots: Absorb water and minerals from the soil.
  • Stem: Serves as the highway, containing Xylem (moves water up) and Phloem (moves food down).
  • Leaves: The site of photosynthesis; they produce the food that needs to be transported to the rest of the plant.

examples.title: The Path of a Sandwich
examples.description: Mouth (Chewing/Saliva) -> Esophagus (Peristalsis) -> Stomach (Acid/Mixing) -> Small Intestine (Absorption) -> Large Intestine (Water recovery) -> Anus (Elimination).

examples.title: Transpiration in Plants
examples.description: Water evaporates from the leaves, creating a 'pull' that draws water all the way from the roots up through the stem.

keyTerms.definition: Wave-like muscle contractions that move food through the digestive tract.
Finger-like projections in the small intestine that increase surface area for absorption.
Plant tissue that transports water and minerals from roots to leaves.

keyConcepts: Digestion involves both mechanical and chemical changes.
Organ systems interact to provide nutrients and remove toxic wastes.
Roots, stems, and leaves are interconnected organs in the plant transport system.
summary: Survival depends on the coordination of organ systems. In humans, the digestive system processes food while working with the excretory system to manage waste. In plants, roots, stems, and leaves function together to transport vital water and nutrients.

What plant tissue is responsible for transporting water upward?
